posts.text: No one should ever answer, "Does Israel have a right to exist?" without asking back, "Does Palestine have a right to exist?" I guarantee you that if you did this on cable news, every cable anchor would panic and literally none of them would say yes to that. Hypocrites and liars.

"Does Israel have a right to exist?" is the dumbest, most disingenuous question. It already exists! Isn't it insane that none of our so-called news reporters ask actual question that makes sense - "Does Palestine have a right to exist?" That's the state being blocked, not Israel.

Imagine if they asked every politician, "Are you a Turkish nationalist?" Wtf?! And the expectation was that you have to say yes! Or, "Are you a Peruvian nationalist?!" Why? Why do I have to be a nationalist for Israel or any other country? What an insane piece of propaganda.

Political "reporters" and "news" anchors keep asking Americans in politics and media, "Are you a Zionist?" What a weird question. Do we have an obligation to be a Zionist? Is that a gotcha question? Do we have to swear allegiance to nationalist ideology of a different country?

The job of the liars in the American media is to keep information like this away from you, so they can keep pretending Israel is doing self-defense. 

The job of our politicians is to finance and provide troops for the expansion of this Israeli Empire.

"Current campaign in Lebanon must end with a fundamental change of situation: the Litani must be our new border with the state of Lebanon, like the Yellow Line in Gaza and like the buffer and the crown of Mount Hermon in Syria." -Smotrich

This was always about land acquisition.

We're going to have Joe Kent on @TheYoungTurks on Thursday (show starts at 6PM ET on YouTube, M-F). Today @nytimes confirmed one claim Kent made: "Israeli officials would probably view a failed Iranian state that is too caught up in internal turmoil to menace Israel as a win." 

In other words, the Israelis are content to create chaos in the Middle East as long as all their neighbors are destroyed. Why? Because they can pick up more territory in the chaos, like they're doing in Lebanon right now

The Saudis and the Israelis both now want us to use our ground troops for the war against their regional competitor. I have a better idea - why don't they use their own ground troops? 

That won't even be discussed in media. They find it outrageous to use precious Israeli troops.

Saudis think the war has made Iran stronger because it's proven their lock on Strait of Hormuz. So, they want us to stay longer to do regime change. And just like the Israelis, I don't give a fuck what the Saudis want. We should make decisions for America's benefit, not theirs.

Very least we could do is vote out all the incumbents. All the people who have already betrayed us and sold us out, not just to Israel, but to all the donors who came by and gave them "campaign contributions." Their experience is in corruption, we should dump almost all of them.

If you back a presidential candidate who takes money from Israeli lobby, you ought to have your head examined. You're literally letting them take our leader, and have them work for Israel instead. That's the whole point of giving them millions of dollars! It's not complicated.

We don't even control our own country. No one wants to be in this war, but we're forced into it by another country that's tiny, but seems to have all of our leaders under their command. It's intolerable. I can't stand the lack of freedom and autonomy. I want our country back.
The only reason we won't do this is because Israel won't give us permission. The rest is just propaganda from our media and politicians to get us to stay longer to serve Israel more.

Here's how we get out of this war - we make a deal with Iran that we stop attacking them, they stop attacking us and our allies in the Gulf and open up the Strait of Hormuz. Then let Israel and Iran fight as long as they like. Not our war, accomplished our goals. Let's come home!

You notice that the minute you ask simple questions, you get labeled a "conspiracy theorist" by traditional media. Are we not allowed to ask about strange occurences? Or should all good "journalists" shut up and write down what the government said! 

It's hilarious to see "reporters" saying you shouldn't ask questions of the government. I didn't come within a country mile of reaching any conclusions. So, it's the very act of questioning the beloved government and the beloved powerful that so off
